issues.description: Two cards in 'Star & Decorative Bullets' section both labelled 'White Star' but render different glyphs (✧ U+2727 vs ☆ U+2606). Confusing for users who can't tell which is which.
Two adjacent cards labelled 'White Star' in the Star & Decorative Bullets row (✧ and ☆) — same labelling collision visible on mobile.

Identical combo ☁️🌙 appears in 'Aesthetic & Vibes' (labelled 'Cloudy night') AND in 'Soft & Cute' (labelled 'Cloud moon'). Same string, two cards, two categories — copies the same character sequence under different names.
Same ☁️🌙 duplicate combo across 'Aesthetic & Vibes' (Cloudy night) and 'Soft & Cute' (Cloud moon) is also visible on mobile.

H1 'S̶t̶r̶i̶k̶e̶t̶h̶r̶o̶u̶g̶h̶ Text Generator' uses combining strikethrough characters that visually extend the strike line slightly into the unstyled 'Text Generator' words because of glyph metrics — looks like the strike crosses into the next word. Acceptable as a creative choice but visually noisy.
On mobile the H1 wraps after 'Strikethrough', so 'Text Generator' renders cleanly on its own line — issue is less pronounced than desktop but still present at the wrap point.

H1 uses fullwidth characters 'ａｅｓｔｈｅｔｉｃ' which are extremely wide; combined with bold display font, the title wraps awkwardly with 'Generator' dropping to its own line on desktop and feels visually heavy compared to other tool pages.
Fullwidth 'ａｅｓｔｈｅｔｉｃ' in H1 forces 'Text Generator' onto a second line on mobile too — title takes 2 lines and feels disproportionately tall.

All four output cards (Upside Down Flipped, Upside Down Same Order, Reversed, Reversed + Spaced) display plain English placeholder text like 'Text flipped both upside down and reversed' instead of the actual transformed/flipped/reversed Unicode preview. By contrast, sibling tools small-text, strikethrough-text and aesthetic-text all show real transformed example output in the empty state. User has no way to see what the tool actually produces without typing — looks like the conversion is broken or the placeholder data was never converted.

Same as desktop: all four output card previews show plain English description text rather than actual mirrored/flipped Unicode output. Empty state is uninformative and looks like the tool is non-functional.
